children: New Delhi, Oct. 12 -- Indian stock market investors are likely to keep an eye on several companies on Tuesday, October 13, after a series of key earnings announcements, order wins, business developments and strategic partnerships.
HCL Technologies, RBL Bank, Azad Engineering, Nazara Technologies, Hindustan Composites and Hexaware Technologies are among the stocks likely to remain in focus.

IRCON International: The railway major secures an EPC contract worth Rs.862.46 crore from East Central Railway for the supply of ballast and permanent way materials, with the project scheduled for completion within 365 days.

Bhagyanagar India: The compnay said it signed an MoU with Om Sree Builders and Developers LLP for the sale of 7,260 square yards of land at IDA Uppal, Hyderabad, for Rs.60 crore. The remaining 12,820.52 square yards will be jointly developed, with the company entitled to 30% of the saleable area, subject to shareholder approval.

ICICI Prudential AMC: The AMC posted Q2 net profit of Rs.889 crore, down 7.9% year-on-year. Total income declines 3.1% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.1,691 crore from Rs.1,745 crore in the previous quarter.

HCL Tech: The technology major reports revenue for the September ending quarter at Rs.35,620 crore, up 3% quarter-on-quarter and 11.5% year-on-year. Advanced AI revenue rises 28.4% sequentially and 78% year-on-year in constant currency terms.

RBL Bank: The private sector lender reported standalone net profit of Rs.482 crore in Q2, up from Rs.179 crore a year earlier. Gross NPAs improves to 1.02% from 1.30% in the previous quarter, while net NPAs decline to 0.29% from 0.37%.

Hindustan Composites: Alongside its September-quarter results, the company declares a special interim dividend of Rs.21 per equity share of Rs.5 face value for FY27. October 16, 2026, is the record date.

Azad Engineering: The defence company secured a two-year long-term rate contract worth approximately Rs.52.68 crore from BHEL for the supply of critical stationary and rotating airfoils for heavy-duty gas turbines.
Hazoor Multi Projects: The company received an updated award letter from NHAI for collecting user fees at Gaddurur Fee Plaza. The contract is worth Rs.28.10 crore and has a tenure of one year.

Nazara Technologies: The company said it Appointed Arun Agrawal as chief financial officer, effective October 16, 2026. The company identified in the final announcement has approved the redesignation of Mithun Padam Sacheti from non-executive director to executive director, subject to shareholder approval.

Whole-time Director Rohit Sharma will step down at the close of business on January 11, 2027, while Nitish Mittersain will transition from managing director to founder and non-executive director, effective at the close of business on October 12, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
